questions.prompt: In what order does data A move when a program loads it from a file?
After A is incremented in a register, A has the same value everywhere in the hierarchy.
In a multitasking environment, what must every process get when it reads A?
options: The most recently updated value, wherever it's stored

questions.prompt: On a multiprocessor, the hardware that makes sure all CPUs' caches have the most recent value is called cache ______. (one word)
Why is cache coherency a problem on multiprocessors but not on a single CPU?
options: Each CPU has its own cache, so one value can be cached in several places at once
It's not a problem on multiprocessors

questions.prompt: Cache coherency on a multiprocessor is usually provided in hardware.
Why are distributed systems even harder?
options: They only have one copy of every datum
Several copies (replicas) of a datum can exist on different computers, connected by a network
